messages:
tara: Quick heads-up: I finished a focused econ+quality sweep for zenith-12b with two precision flavors: int8 baseline and "int5-ec" (experimental compaction with KF cache). Posting concise findings and a staging routing suggestion for GTN.

mike: appreciate it. Product needs a single-paragraph recommendation and a realistic $ example.

jess: drop the core numbers plz. keep it short.

tara: core mixed-traffic numbers (median prompt 56 tok):
- int8 baseline: p50 105ms, p95 270ms, throughput 240 tok/s, unit cost = $0.013/token-eq
- int5-ec: p50 118ms, p95 330ms, throughput 290 tok/s, unit cost = $0.0082/token-eq (~37% cheaper)
quality quick-check (GTN slices aggregated):
- short QA EM: int8 79.6%, int5-ec 78.4% (delta -1.2 pts, bootstrap CI +/-0.6)
- rerank NDCG proxy: int8 0.713, int5-ec 0.709 (-0.6%)
- long summary ROUGE proxy: int8 0.61, int5-ec 0.57 (-6.6%), variance higher (longform n=900)
- hallucination proxy: int8 3.9%, int5-ec 4.5%
sample: 7.5k queries across 10 customer slices; longform slice small => high variance.

omar: That longform drop is notable. Any idea where errors concentrate?

tara: mostly on multi-step reasoning prompts and certain priming patterns with many examples in-context. Short, template-driven prompts (snippets, rerank) show tiny diffs. int5-ec gains amplify when prefix reuse/kvcache hits because token cost lower and cache hit rate higher.

eva: ops question: why p95 jumps for int5-ec?

tara: kernel path: int5-ec uses a new emulation path for rare token widths -> some sequences hit a slow fallback kernel. ops tuning (batch shape + fused-attn flag) should shave ~40-60ms p95. we'll open ticket.

ops-bot: ticket created #KERNEL-5582 (owner: @omar) to investigate int5-ec fallback path and batch tuning. ETA 3d.

mike: draft routing suggestion for product/GTN? they want conservative default but cost upside.

tara: draft routing rules (short):
```
routes:
  - name: short-primary
    match: intent in ["search_snippet","rerank","qa_short"]
    split: { int5-ec: 0.65, int8: 0.35 }
  - name: convo-default
    match: intent in ["assistant_chat","user_short_session"]
    split: { int5-ec: 0.4, int8: 0.6 }
  - name: longform-safe
    match: intent in ["summarize_long","doc_analysis","chain_of_thought"]
    split: { int8: 1.0 }
canary: 1% for 1h -> 5% for 3h -> 25% for 12h, require stable QA_EM and latency_p95
rollbacks:
  - if QA_EM drops > 1.5 pts absolute on any slice over 30m -> rollback that slice
  - if hallucination_rate +0.8% abs -> rollback
monitor: ["QA_EM","NDCG_proxy","hallucination_rate","latency_p95","cost_per_1k_tokens"]
```

jess: solid. now the $ example for GTN: pick a mid-market (30M tok/mo) and an enterprise (100M tok/mo, 30% longform).

tara: quick math:
- Mid-market 30M tokens/mo, if 70% eligible -> 21M * (0.013 - 0.0082) = $102.9k/mo gross; realistic eligible share ~60% -> ~$88k/mo
- Enterprise 100M tok/mo with 30% longform -> eligible = 70M * (0.013 - 0.0082) = $336k/mo gross; realistic ~60% eligible -> ~$201k/mo
notes: assumes billed token-eq consistent; priming-heavy workloads may see different savings.

omar: action items?

tara: 1) ops (#KERNEL-5582) tune int5-ec kernel & batch shapes (owner: omar). 2) jess run 2-day slice A/B on longform (20k samples) to tighten CI. 3) tara post GTN note with bullets and comms draft. 4) eva prepare customer-facing FAQ + opt-out for longform.

eva: will draft comms and opt-out form.

mike: product bullet (one-liner) for GTN: "Recommend introducing an experimental low-precision tier (int5-ec) for short-form and high-volume rerank traffic to reduce token unit costs ~37% while preserving near-parity on short QA and rerank; longform remains on int8 pending additional evals and kernel tuning."

tara: I'll post the GTN note in 40m and attach per-slice CSVs. thanks all :thumbsup:
